text:
alejandra: Quick heads-up — Tom (customer) doing a private-VPC POC. Hits intermittent TLS handshake failures when routing through their edge NAT/proxy to our Private Endpoint. Can someone swarm? cc @mike_s @noah

Tom (customer): Here's the error from their app:
```
2026-03-21T14:02:12Z ERROR api_request: tls: handshake failure
remote_addr=10.0.2.5:43210 target=redwood-private-endpoint.internal:443
```
Also tried curl and got `SSL: no alternative certificate`

mike_s: OK — first suspects: SNI rewrite by their proxy or wrong DNS (resolving to an intermediary). Tom, can you paste the output of:
`dig +short redwood-private-endpoint.internal @<their-resolver>`
and
`openssl s_client -connect <resolved-ip>:443 -servername redwood-private.sni.example.com -showcerts`

Tom (customer): dig returns `10.10.11.22` (internal NLB), openssl shows server cert CN=*.edge-corp.internal, not our cert. Output:
```
CONNECTED(00000003)
depth=0 CN = *.edge-corp.internal
verify error:num=20:unable to get local issuer certificate
---
Certificate chain
 0 s:/CN=*.edge-corp.internal
   i:/CN=internal-ca
---
```
So looks like a TLS-terminating proxy in front of the endpoint.

mike_s: That matches SNI/termination. Two things to confirm:
- Are they using a PrivateLink/Interface endpoint or an internal NLB + proxy? PrivateLink should route directly to our ENI and present our certificate. NLB+proxy can terminate TLS.
- Check their iptables/NAT hairpin rules — traffic from inside VPC to NLB can hit a proxy path that breaks SNI.

noah: +1. From network side: if DNS for the private hostname points to their internal appliance, appliance may do TLS termination or mTLS. Ask them to run `tcpdump -nni any port 443` during a failed request and share the SYN/SYN-ACK sequence. Also confirm whether their proxy rewrites the Host or SNI fields.

Tom (customer): Will try tcpdump. One more oddity — our client sometimes gets a 403 with `tls: bad certificate` after a few minutes. Could cert pinning conflict?

mike_s: 403 + bad certificate sounds like our SDK attempted to fallback to a different route (maybe public endpoint) and the proxy returns a management page cert. Can you check the full HTTP response headers and the TLS ServerName used? A curl -v will show `Server certificate` and `Server name` negotiation.

Tom (customer): curl -v shows `Server name: redwood-private.sni.example.com` but certificate CN is `portal.edge-corp.internal`. Header `Via: 1.1 appliance` present.

alejandra: Filing this as a blocker for our enterprise POC. Customer is worried about data path and certs. Any mitigations we can offer short-term so they can demo?

noah: Short term options:
- Ask them to enable TCP pass-through on appliance for the redwood hostname (no TLS termination).
- As a workaround, create an internal DNS override that resolves the hostname to our PrivateLink ENI IP directly on their resolver.
- If they must terminate, have them present a SAN that includes our expected hostname and use a cert chain we can validate (not ideal).

mike_s: I'll draft an internal cert/policy note for them. Also confirm whether their egress firewall is doing TLS-inspection (MITM) — that would explain alternate certs and intermittent behavior.

jen_oncall: I've opened an internal incident: INC-2026-1875, assigned to net+sec. Escalation notes: POC blocked, possible TLS interception at customer edge, needs packet captures and DNS trace. ETA 2h. :rotating_light:

infra-bot: support-bot: Created ticket #POC-4621. Linked to INC-2026-1875. Notifying oncall rotation.

mike_s: Tom — when you have the tcpdump, please DM me encrypted link. Also include `dig +trace` to show which resolver is authoritative for the override. If you can't run tcpdump, an `ssldump` or `tshark -w` pcap will work.

Tom (customer): Uploading pcap to the share now. One quick Q: does Redwood accept client certs for mutual-TLS on Private endpoints? They could configure appliance to pass client certs through.

alejandra: We support mTLS on Dedicated/Private with proper onboarding — we can discuss in the support ticket. For POC, simpler to avoid TLS termination in their appliance.

noah: Follow-up checklist for triage:
1) confirm DNS: `dig` from app host to resolver, `dig +trace` to validate override
2) packet capture showing TLS ClientHello SNI and ServerHello cert
3) confirm whether their appliance rewrites Host header or sets Via
4) test direct connect to PrivateLink ENI IP (bypass appliance) — if that works, it's definitely the appliance
5) firewall rules: ensure NAT hairpin allowed for internal-to-internal NLB

alejandra: Thanks team. I'll coordinate with the customer and keep the ticket updated. Will post when we have the pcap. :thumbsup:

Tom (customer): Uploaded pcap link: https://files.corp.example/poc/pcap/1923456780.pcap - markers at 14:01 and 14:03 for failed flows.

mike_s: Got it, pulling pcap. Quick note — if customer can't change appliance rules, we can propose a short-term private DNS override that points to a dedicated test ENI we control, so they can demo without TLS interception. I'll add that option to the ticket.

jen_oncall: INC updated with pcap and proposed mitigation. Keeping blocked status until we validate.

alejandra: Great. Keeping this thread as the single comms channel for the POC. If anyone notices new errors (rate limits, token issues) call it out here.
